reuse.why: The API and existing planning consumers reuse getScheduledAmount, which also reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance helper.

duplication.why: Range selection and approximate-amount planning remain centralized without introducing duplicated calculation blocks.

placement.why: Planning policy stays in shared schedule logic, while API serialization and consumer-specific data extraction remain in their existing layers.

scope.why: The changes focus on schedule amount planning, its API representation, and accompanying tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared implementation is straightforward, although an optional string operator behind a positional boolean makes the helper contract less explicit.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Changed consumers consistently call getScheduledAmount rather than implementing their own planning calculations.

disguised_duplication.where: No copied or reshaped calculation logic is introduced.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains the op parameter in place of rangeRounding and an isapprox branch; both represent required domain variation, with no new bypassing consumers.
